title: What is known about 1RB0LA_0RC1RF_0LD1RE_1LA0RB_0RD---_1RA1RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LA_0RC1RF_0LD1RE_1LA0RB_0RD---_1RA1RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

The tape is a list of numbers written in two ways. When the head is at the right end, they are runs of 1s separated by single 0s (1^4 0 1^8 0 1^5 0 1^23 0 …); when it is at the left end, the same numbers are gaps of 0s between single 1s (1 0^4 1 0^8 1 0^5 1 0^23 …). State A, running left over a run of 1s, erases it (Lean: (1)^n A> 1 becomes A> 1 (0)^n), and the sweep right writes the runs back. The left end is a run A>0 0 (10)^n lengthened by one at each visit (45 to 48 between steps 7.4·108 and 1.5·109); the right end is one run of 1s lengthened by one at each new cell on the right (34 to 38 in the same stretch). In between, the list changes slowly and irregularly.
verdict: The question is open. The machine can halt only from B> 0 1 1 (proved in Lean); in 20,000,000,000 steps that never happens. In the first 109 steps B had 1 0 1 ahead 25 times and 1 1 0 10 times (the last at step 740,088,686, just after a visit to the left end), and never 0 1 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 218 cells have been visited and 65 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.074). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.125).

claims.title: The halting context
claims.text: From B> 0 1 1 the machine reaches its halting transition (proved step by step, then step_none_iff). The halting transition is E reading a 1. E is entered only from C reading a 1 (C writes 1 and moves right), and C only from B reading a 0 (B writes 0 and moves right).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: 8 shift rules over the words of the tape (for example (1)^n A> 1 becomes A> 1 (0)^n in n steps and B> (100)^n becomes (111)^n B> in 3n steps), proved for every n.

claims.title: No halt in the first 20,000,000,000 steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun.c runs 20,000,000,000 steps without a halt; the visited tape is 254 cells wide and holds 66 ones.

claims.title: Near misses
claims.text: In the first 109 steps B had 1 0 1 ahead 25 times and 1 1 0 10 times (the last at step 740,088,686, just after a visit to the left end), and never 0 1 1.

claims.title: Growth
claims.text: The left run of 10 and the right run of 1s each gain one copy per visit of the head to that end, and the visits come at exponentially spaced times.

claims.title: 40 event rules for every size
claims.text: From an event (A on the start cell) to the next: the 4-step A> 0 0 0 0 → A> 1 1 0 0, the 18-step 0 0 A> 1 1 0^7 → 0 1 A> 0^6 1 0 0, and 38 longer ones with up to two repeat counts, each proved for every value of its counts.

claims.title: Coverage: 99.98% of the events
claims.text: 101,546,466 events in 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps, 18,500 not matched by a rule. The three most frequent rules fire 50,773,233, 16,777,216 (= 2<sup>24</sup>) and 8,388,597 times.

claims.title: B> 0 1 1 never occurs
claims.text: In 3·109 steps B never has 0 1 1 ahead.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Halting needs B to meet 0 1 1; the list keeps every 1-run followed by a 0 where B could meet one, but without the rule of the list this is not proved.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is a list of numbers that the head rewrites from runs of 1s into gaps of 0s and back; around the start cell it works like a binary counter, and all but 0.02% of its events there follow rules proved for every size. The one way to stop has never come up.

facts.text: Event rules proved in Lean for every size.
Of the 101,546,466 events of 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps follow them.
From it the machine halts (Lean halt_ctx); every halt passes through it (from the table).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.074). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.125).
After 109 steps the tape spans 218 cells (87 left of the start, 123 right), with a density of 1s of 0.298.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: The one way to stop
html: The halting transition is E reading a 1. E is entered only from C reading a 1 (C writes 1 and moves right), and C only from B reading a 0 (B writes 0 and moves right). So the machine halts exactly when it produces B> 0 1 1; Lean proves the steps from there to the halt (halt_ctx).

sections.heading: What a proof would need
html: Not known. Halting needs B to meet 0 1 1; the list keeps every 1-run followed by a 0 where B could meet one, but without the rule of the list this is not proved.

The basic moves are proved in Lean for every length (lean/Rules.lean: crossing a run of one word in a fixed number of steps per copy), so a proof would need only the rule of the counter on top of them.

summary: A two-way list of numbers (runs of 1s going right, gaps of 0s going left) with a binary-counter-like engine at the start cell; 40 event rules (A on cell 0) proved for all sizes cover 99.98% of 1.0·10^8 events in 3·10^9 steps; B> 0 1 1 (from it the machine halts) never occurs.
